decisions.reason: As a close-to-core finish variant with low carrying costs, it is worth keeping while it continues to complement the main range even if demand proves only moderate.

This shower channel remains well aligned with the firm’s established technical and architectural offering, so the option value of staying in seamless bathroom designs still exceeds the limited cost of continuation.

The pump-assisted line is still more uncertain and resource-intensive than standard drains, but its relevance for difficult installation cases and barrier-free bathrooms justifies keeping it one year longer.
As a complementary design grate close to the core range, it likely stays because it broadens choice at modest cost and does not tie up much additional resource.

Because this newer pump-drain channel is strategically relevant yet still early and somewhat overlapping with other pump solutions, management would likely keep it for now but with a clearly higher exit risk than standard products.
